title: Streaming heartbeat timeouts causing cascading 5xxs for large-client workloads — mitigation and permanent fix
creator: Amaya Chen
description: High-severity escalation from two enterprise customers (ACME & BlueSky) reporting periodic waves of 5xxs and aborted streaming responses during long-running sessions. Initial blameless triage shows correlation with long-lived streaming connections that intermittently pause on client-side for >30s (e.g., user backgrounding or network flaps). These pauses combined with current keepalive/heartbeat defaults and server-side read blocking caused worker-thread pileups and amplified retries, producing customer-visible 5xx spikes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a long-running streaming request against hosted API with chunked responses (simulate 60s+ session).
2) Pause the client socket reads for 40s (simulate mobile background).
3) Resume reads. Observe: server-side streaming stalls, request appears hung, upstream retries from SDK increase, connection resets follow and 5xxs spike.
4) Reproduce at scale by running 100 concurrent clients with randomized pause windows to trigger worker-thread exhaustion and proxy queueing.

2025-06-11 - Instrumented per-connection socket metrics, added streaming-latency SLI, and created Grafana dashboard.
2025-06-12 18:40 UTC - Deployed hotfix v2025.06.12: edge-level synthetic heartbeats + conservative connection admission cap for affected pools; customer errors dropped by ~78%.

root_cause: A combination of client-side long pauses during streaming plus edge and runtime defaults led to server worker threads blocked on socket reads and stalled KV-cache handling. The stalled workers delayed processing of other tenants' requests, causing retries to pile up, TCP backpressure at the proxy, and ultimately 5xx responses when timeouts and resource exhaustion were reached.
proposed_fix_summary: Introduce per-pool adaptive admission control for active streaming sessions, add lightweight in-proxy synthetic heartbeats to avoid socket-level closure during moderate pauses, and change server read timeout semantics to fail fast for stalled streams while returning structured retryable error codes. Also add SDK guidance for keepalive and backoff to avoid retry amplification.
implementation_plan: 1) Implement admission controller in serving runtime: configurable max concurrent streaming sessions per tenant and global pool with queueing (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427).

2) In edge proxy (envoy config): add optional synthetic ping frames for streaming connections and align upstream read timeouts with runtime fail-fast policy (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-config/pull/89).
3) Modify SDKs to respect server-provided Retry-After headers and use jittered exponential backoff for streaming reconnects (SDK issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/603).
4) Add runtime metric k_streaming_blocked_seconds and alert if > 1% of workers blocked for >15s.
5) QA: end-to-end test harness that simulates large-client background/foreground cycles and validates no amplification at 200x concurrency.
rollout_plan: Canary (10% of edge pools) - deploy admission controller + synthetic heartbeats to non-production tenants first.
Monitor: per-tenant streaming error rate, worker-blocked metric, proxy queue depth. Hold for 2 full production cycles (48h).
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 40% -> 100% in 6-hour increments if metrics stable.
Customer opt-in: give ACME/BlueSky the option for early enablement and test with their traffic windows.
Fallback: feature flag to disable synthetic heartbeats and admission caps; rollback path tested in runbook.
verification_checks: Synthetic traffic test: 200 concurrent simulated streams with randomized 10-60s pause windows show <1% 5xx and no worker-blocked alerts.
Grafana panels: streaming_error_rate < baseline + 0.5% for 48h after full rollout.
Tracing: percent of streaming traces that include 'admission-queued' tag should be <5% during normal traffic and <25% under peak.
Customer confirmation: ACME & BlueSky confirm no visible errors during their test windows.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add explicit streaming SLO and runbook entries for mobile-client backgrounding patterns.
2) Ship SDK patch to reduce aggressive reconnects for streaming clients within 48h of rollout completion.
3) Create tenant-facing KB article on best practices for long-running streams.
4) Add automated chaos tests in CI that simulate paused clients and verify no cross-tenant degradation.
